_readme: Smart Order V2 curated Smart Picks dataset. Smart Picks are analyzed selections, not complete restaurant menus. data_status describes source quality, freshness and field coverage. Keep unknown values null, never 0.
tips: Sauce is the quietest calorie source on the menu. A single dipping cup runs 100–200 cal and 5–10g sugar. Ask for it on the side and use half.
Cheese adds roughly 90–120 cal, 8g fat and 200mg sodium per slice or scoop. It's the single easiest thing to drop.
Fries are almost never worth it here. A medium adds 350–450 cal and turns a reasonable order into a heavy one. A side salad or fruit cup is a 200–400 cal swing.
A medium regular soda is 200–300 cal of pure sugar and doesn't fill you up. Unsweet tea, diet, or water is the biggest single win on the whole order.
Grilled beats crispy every time — usually 150–250 fewer calories and about half the fat for the same protein.
Sodium is the hardest target in fast food. Almost nothing clears 600mg once it has bread, cheese and sauce. Bowls and salads are where you'll find it.
Skipping the bun cuts about 120–200 cal and 25–35g carbs, and most places will serve it in a bowl or lettuce wrap if you ask.

chains.name: Chipotle
tips: Build a bowl, not a burrito. The tortilla alone is about 320 cal and 50g carbs.
Fajita veggies instead of rice keeps the bowl full-sized for almost no calories.
Sodium is the weak spot. Salsas carry 200–550mg each — pick one, not three.

chains.name: In-N-Out Burger
tips: Protein Style is the highest-impact swap here: replacing the bun with lettuce cuts a large chunk of carbs and calories.
If sodium is the priority, the Protein Style Hamburger is the standout among the burgers in this set.
Fries are a full 360 calories, so the burger choice matters less if fries automatically come along for the ride.

methodology.smart_picks: Restaurant entries are curated choices analyzed by Smart Order, not claims of full-menu coverage.
methodology.missing_data: Unknown nutrition values are stored as null and are never treated as zero.
methodology.net_carbs: net_carbs_g is a derived comparison field where source data supports the calculation; it should not be presented as restaurant-certified unless explicitly published.
methodology.verification: Verified means every listed Smart Pick for that chain was checked against a current official source and all required macro fields are populated.
